title: A sink is a parameter that becomes an instruction, and an unclassified one refuses
scope:

sink; the fail-closed default for a `string`/`bytes` parameter nobody classified, and where that
classification is declared; which sink `echo` writes to in every execution context Novis has; the typed

summary.headline: A sink is any parameter that becomes an instruction; unclassified ones refuse
summary.body:
A built-in parameter is a sink when its content becomes an instruction something executes — a
query, a template, a command line — rather than data something returns. There is no list to fall
behind: a built-in text or bytes parameter nobody has classified refuses untrusted input, so a
`printf` template cannot quietly accept what a query cannot. Every context has an output sink
and the default is the terminal, so `echo` in a scheduled script or a job worker neutralizes
control bytes; only an HTTP request attaches the HTML sink.
